cases.title: Bitwise operators & | ^ ~ << >>
cases.notes: One operator per wrong file on Uint<8>: & | ^ << >> ~. & and | are lexer errors: the lexer wants && or ||, so it reports the next character ("unexpected character ' '", or 'b' when written a&b). ^ and ~ are unexpected characters. << and >> are parse errors that mention an internal grammar name, expression4. A probe of & on Field gives the same message. What Compact does offer: Boolean &&, ||, ! and != ; Bytes<n> indexing (b[0] is a Uint<8>) and a cast from Bytes<n> to Vector<n, Uint<8>>; no cast from Uint to Vector<n, Boolean>. right.compact keeps flags as Vector<8, Boolean> and maps &&, ||, != and ! over them. right2.compact replaces a << 3 with (a * 8) as Uint<16> (widened, so unlike a fixed-width shift nothing is truncated). right3.compact replaces a >> 3 with a witness quotient and remainder checked by r < 8 and q * 8 + r == a. All three change representation or move work to a witness.

cases.title: Recursive circuit call
cases.notes: Settled: both compilers print `recursion involving factorial`, which matches the compiler-errors.md template `recursion involving~?`; the text `recursive circuit call` (compilation-review.md) never appears. The catalogue snippet verbatim (`return n * factorial(n - 1);` with Uint<64>) does not reach the recursion check: both compilers first report `mismatch between actual return type Uint<0..340282366920938463426481119284349108226> and declared return type Uint<64> of circuit factorial`, so wrong.compact casts the product back to Uint<64>.
